key_insight: A thermal scanning probe can directly write individual CsPbI3 quantum dots with atomic-scale placement, enabling deterministic single-photon emitters.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route to integrate colloidal quantum dots with photonic devices on demand, overcoming the usual randomness of solution-based deposition.
method: Used a nanoscale-confined thermal scanning probe to localize QD formation volume.
Achieved site-selective synthesis with <25 nm spatial control, down to a single atomic-scale QD.
Coupled written emitters to photonic cavities to test emission enhancement.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports high-yield arrays of CsPbI3 emitters with narrow linewidths, up to 98% single-photon purity at room temperature, and enhanced spontaneous emission in cavities.
watch_item: The approach likely depends on precise thermal probe control and material stability, so scalability and reproducibility across larger device areas may be challenging.
paper_title: Direct writing of individual quantum dots
